records.source: Κἀγώ, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἠδυνήθην λαλῆσαι ὑμῖν ὡς πνευματικοῖς ἀλλ’ ὡς σαρκίνοις, ὡς νηπίοις ἐν Χριστῷ.
records.gloss: And I, brothers, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual [ones] but as to fleshy [ones], as to infants in Christ.
pieces: As for me, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I could not speak to you as people of the Spirit. I had to speak to you as people of mere flesh, as infants in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.1: And I, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual [people], but as to [people] of flesh, as to infants in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.1: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, when I was with you, I could not talk to you as people who are led by God's Spirit. I had to talk to you as people who still thought in merely human ways. You were like babies in your new life with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: fellow believers, women and men
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοί addresses the whole church at Corinth, which included women (7:1-16; 11:5), as it does in 1:10, 1:26 and 2:1.

decisions.choice: people of the Spirit: those whose thinking is shaped by God's Spirit
alternatives: spiritual in the sense of religious or devout
decisions.reason: πνευματικοῖς picks up 2:13-15, where the person of the Spirit receives what God's Spirit teaches and can judge all things. Paul is not contrasting soul and body but life led by the Spirit with life on a merely human level.

decisions.choice: people of flesh: still living on a merely human level, as new believers do
alternatives: sinful in character (the sense of the related word in verse 3)
decisions.reason: σαρκίνοις describes what is made of flesh. Paul uses it here of the Corinthians when he first came, when their immaturity was to be expected. In verse 3 he switches to a related word that describes a character shaped by the flesh, and that is a reproach: they should have grown out of it by now.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "of flesh" (the word for what is made of flesh)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read here the same word as in verse 3. The two words look alike and differ in sense only a little; the earlier reading lets Paul move from a description (verse 1) to a reproach (verse 3). Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: infants in Christ: real believers, but immature
alternatives: people not yet in Christ at all
decisions.reason: "In Christ" means they truly belong to Christ (1:2, 1:30); νηπίοις says only that they were very young in that life. Compare "mature" in 2:6 and the call to grow up in 14:20.

decisions.choice: Paul looks back to his first stay in Corinth
decisions.reason: ἠδυνήθην is a past tense: when Paul first preached in Corinth (2:1-5; Acts 18:1-11) he could not yet speak to them as mature believers. Verse 2 adds that even now they are not ready.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul is addressing the whole church, women and men; the traditional form is one tap away.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: people of the Spirit; people of mere flesh
decisions.reason: "Spiritual" in current English often means devout or interested in religion, and "carnal" is now mostly about sex. Balanced names the Spirit and the flesh, the two sides Paul is contrasting (m2, m3). "Worldly" is avoided because it would blur this word with the Greek word for the world (verse 19).

decisions.choice: when I was with you; still thought in merely human ways; babies in your new life with Christ
alternatives: I could not speak to you; as fleshly people; infants in Christ
decisions.reason: Readable says when this was (m6), puts "of flesh" in plain words (m3), and explains "infants in Christ" (m5).

records.heading: Still infants

records.source: γάλα ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα, οὐ βρῶμα, οὔπω γὰρ ἐδύνασθε.
records.gloss: Milk you I gave to drink, not food, for not yet were you able.
pieces: Milk was what I gave you to drink, not solid food, since you could not yet take it.

L.2: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able [to take it].

R.2: I fed you with milk, the way people feed a baby. I did not give you solid food, because you could not handle it yet.

decisions.choice: milk and solid food: the first, simple teaching and the fuller teaching that the mature can take
alternatives: two different messages, one for beginners and one for an inner circle
decisions.reason: The picture follows from "infants" in verse 1. Milk is not a different gospel: Paul preached Christ crucified (2:2), and the "wisdom among the mature" of 2:6 is the same message understood more deeply. Hebrews 5:12-14 and 1 Peter 2:2 use the same picture.

decisions.choice: one verb, "gave to drink", serves for both milk and food
decisions.reason: ἐπότισα means to give someone a drink. Paul lets it cover the food as well, a natural shortcut in Greek; the sense is simply "I fed you".

decisions.choice: you were not yet able: to take solid food
decisions.reason: ἐδύνασθε has no object; from the picture it means they could not yet take in fuller teaching.

decisions.choice: [to take it] (L); take it (B); handle it (R)
decisions.reason: English needs to say what they were not able to do (m3).

decisions.choice: the way people feed a baby
decisions.reason: Readable ties the milk back to the babies of verse 1, so that the picture is clear.

records.source: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν δύνασθε, ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε.
records.gloss: But not even still now are you able, \v 3 for still fleshly you are.
pieces: In fact, even now you still cannot take it,
because you are still living by the flesh.

L.2: Indeed, not even now are you able,

R.2: And even now you are not ready,
R.3: because you are still living in merely human ways.

decisions.choice: indeed not even: the clause sharpens what came before rather than contrasting with it
decisions.reason: The words heighten the point: not only then, but even now.

decisions.choice: fleshly: living by the outlook of human nature apart from God, rather than by the Spirit
alternatives: made of flesh, simply immature (the word in verse 1)
decisions.reason: σαρκικοί describes a character shaped by the flesh. In Galatians 5:19-21 jealousy and strife are among the works of the flesh, and verse 3 names exactly these. This is a reproach: by now they should have grown up.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "not even still now"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack the first "still". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: living by the flesh
decisions.reason: "Worldly" would blur this word with the Greek word for the world (verse 19), and "carnal" now suggests sexual sin. "Living by the flesh" keeps Paul's contrast with the Spirit. Literal keeps the adjective "fleshly".

records.source: ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις, οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε;
records.gloss: For where among you [there is] jealousy and strife, not fleshly are you and according to man walking?
pieces: For as long as there is jealousy and quarreling among you, are you not living by the flesh and behaving in a merely human way?

L.3: For where [there is] jealousy and strife among you, are you not fleshly, and walking according to [a] human [way]?

R.3: You are jealous of each other and you quarrel. Does that not show that you are living in merely human ways? You are behaving as if you did not have God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: where: since, as long as
decisions.reason: ὅπου here gives the ground for the question: as long as these things are found among them, the answer is plain.

decisions.choice: jealousy and strife: rivalry and quarreling between groups
decisions.reason: ζῆλος is jealous rivalry and ἔρις is quarreling; Chloe's people had reported such quarrels (1:11). Both appear among the works of the flesh in Galatians 5:20.

decisions.choice: walking according to man: living by merely human standards, as people without the Spirit live
alternatives: walking about in an ordinary way
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a common Hebrew and Greek way of saying "live, conduct oneself" (Colossians 1:10). "According to man" means by human standards, as opposed to the Spirit (2:14).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "jealousy and strife"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "and divisions" after strife, a word Paul uses in a similar list in Galatians 5:20. The SBLGNT prints the shorter text. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: quarreling; behaving
decisions.reason: "Strife" is now rare in speech, and "walking" in this sense is church language; Balanced uses everyday words (m3).

decisions.choice: You are behaving as if you did not have God's Spirit.
alternatives: You are walking according to man.
decisions.reason: Readable explains "according to man" by the contrast Paul draws in 2:14 and 3:1. It says "as if" because they do have the Spirit (3:16).

records.source: ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ τις· Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, ἕτερος δέ· Ἐγὼ Ἀπολλῶ, οὐκ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε;
records.gloss: For whenever says someone, I on the one hand am of Paul, and another, I of Apollos, not human beings are you?
pieces: When one of you says, "I am for Paul," and another, "I am for Apollos," is that not how people talk who live on a merely human level?

L.4: For whenever someone says, "I am of Paul," and another, "I [am] of Apollos," are you not [mere] human beings?

R.4: One of you says, "I am on Paul's side." Another says, "I am on Apollos's side." When you talk like that, you are acting like people who are only human, as if God's Spirit were not in you.

decisions.choice: of Paul, of Apollos: party slogans saying whose side a person is on
decisions.reason: The names stand in the genitive, saying whose side a person is on. These are two of the slogans quoted in 1:12.

decisions.choice: Apollos: a Jewish teacher from Alexandria who taught in Corinth after Paul
decisions.reason: Acts 18:24-28 describes him as eloquent and strong in the Scriptures; he went to Corinth after Paul had founded the church (Acts 19:1). Paul speaks of him as a fellow worker, not a rival (16:12).

decisions.choice: human beings: merely human, people living without the Spirit
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωποί picks up "according to man" in verse 3. The contrast is with the person of the Spirit (2:15).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "human beings"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "fleshly" here, repeating verse 3. The meaning is close. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: I am for Paul (B); I am on Paul's side (R)
decisions.reason: "I am of Paul" is not natural English; Balanced and Readable say what the slogan means (m1), in the same words as 1:12.

decisions.choice: how people talk who live on a merely human level (B); as if God's Spirit were not in you (R)
decisions.reason: "Are you not human beings?" would sound like a simple fact. Balanced and Readable say what "human" means here (m3).

records.source: Τί οὖν ἐστιν Ἀπολλῶς;
records.gloss: What then is Apollos?
pieces: What, then, is Apollos?

decisions.choice: what: Paul asks about their role, not who they are
decisions.reason: Τί is neuter. Paul asks what Apollos and he are, and answers with a task: servants (verse 5).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "What then is Apollos? And what is Paul?"
alternatives: "Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos?"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "who" and name Paul first. The earlier reading puts Apollos first and asks about function. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

records.source: τί δέ ἐστιν Παῦλος;
records.gloss: And what is Paul?
pieces: And what is Paul?

decisions.choice: Paul speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: Naming himself in the third person, Paul puts himself on the same footing as Apollos: neither is the head of a party.

records.source: διάκονοι δι’ ὧν ἐπιστεύσατε, καὶ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ κύριος ἔδωκεν.
records.gloss: Servants through whom you believed, and to each as the Lord gave.
pieces: Servants through whom you came to believe, each doing the work the Lord assigned.

L.5: Servants through whom you believed, and [each] as the Lord gave to each.

R.5: We are only servants. Through us you came to believe. Each of us did the work the Lord gave him to do.

decisions.choice: servants: people who carry out a task for someone else
decisions.reason: διάκονοι is the general word for someone who serves; the point is that Paul and Apollos work for another, the Lord. Compare Colossians 1:7 and 1:23.

decisions.choice: you believed: you came to faith
decisions.reason: The past tense looks to the time they first believed, through Paul's preaching and Apollos's teaching.

decisions.choice: to each: to each servant, his task
alternatives: to each of you, his faith
decisions.reason: "Each" could be each believer, to whom the Lord gave faith (compare Romans 12:3). But verses 6-8 go on with each worker's task and each worker's reward, so each servant is meant.

decisions.choice: the Lord: most likely Christ
decisions.reason: Paul usually calls Christ "the Lord" (1:2, 1:31), and the servants are servants of Christ (4:1). But verses 6-7 speak of God giving the growth, so God is possible. The sense hardly changes.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "servants"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a word before "servants": "[nothing] but servants". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: each doing the work the Lord assigned (B); Each of us did the work the Lord gave him to do (R)
alternatives: and to each as the Lord gave
decisions.reason: The Greek is very short. Balanced and Readable say what the Lord gave (m3). "Him" is each servant, here Paul and Apollos.

decisions.choice: We are only servants.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the answer a full sentence.

records.source: ἐγὼ ἐφύτευσα, Ἀπολλῶς ἐπότισεν, ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς ηὔξανεν·
records.gloss: I planted, Apollos watered, but the God was causing to grow;
pieces: I planted, Apollos watered, but it was God who kept making it grow.

L.6: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was causing [it] to grow.

R.6: I put the seed in the ground, and Apollos watered it. But God was the one who made it grow.

decisions.choice: planting and watering: Paul founded the church, Apollos built it up
decisions.reason: Paul brought the gospel to Corinth first (Acts 18:1-11); Apollos came later and helped those who had believed (Acts 18:27-28).

decisions.choice: Paul and Apollos did their work once; God was making it grow all along
decisions.reason: ἐφύτευσα and ἐπότισεν are simple past tenses, while ηὔξανεν describes ongoing action. The growth was God's work the whole time.

decisions.choice: kept making it grow (B); made it grow (R)
decisions.reason: "It" is the crop, the church. Balanced brings out the ongoing tense (m2).

decisions.choice: put the seed in the ground
decisions.reason: Readable says what planting means, so that young readers follow the picture.

records.source: ὥστε οὔτε ὁ φυτεύων ἐστίν τι οὔτε ὁ ποτίζων, ἀλλ’ ὁ αὐξάνων θεός.
records.gloss: So that neither the [one] planting is anything nor the [one] watering, but the [one] causing to grow, God.
pieces: So the one who plants does not count for anything, nor does the one who waters. What counts is God, who gives the growth.

L.7: So neither the one planting is anything, nor the one watering, but God, the one causing growth.

R.7: So the person who plants is not important, and neither is the person who waters. God is the one who matters, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes things grow.

decisions.choice: is anything: counts for anything, compared with God
decisions.reason: ἐστίν τι means "is something", "matters". The comparison is with God; verse 8 shows that the workers still have a task and a reward.

decisions.choice: but God, who causes the growth: the verb "is" is understood
decisions.reason: The sentence ends without a verb: what counts is God, the one who makes the growth happen.

decisions.choice: does not count for anything
decisions.reason: "Is nothing" could sound like contempt for the workers; the point is their importance next to God (m1).

decisions.choice: because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes things grow
decisions.reason: Readable turns the participle into a reason, which is what it implies.

records.source: ὁ φυτεύων δὲ καὶ ὁ ποτίζων ἕν εἰσιν, ἕκαστος δὲ τὸν ἴδιον μισθὸν λήμψεται κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον κόπον, θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί· θεοῦ γεώργιον, θεοῦ οἰκοδομή ἐστε.
records.gloss: The [one] planting and the [one] watering one are, and each the own wage will receive according to the own labor. \v 9 For of God we are fellow workers; of God [a] field, of God [a] building you are.
pieces: The one who plants and the one who waters work as one, and each will be rewarded according to the labor each has done.
For we are fellow workers in God's service, and you are God's field, God's building.

L.8: Now the one planting and the one watering are one, and each will receive {{gender:their|his}} own wage according to {{gender:their|his}} own labor.
L.9: For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's field, God's building.

R.8: The one who plants and the one who waters work together for the same purpose. God will reward each of them for the hard work they have done.
R.9: We are workers who work together for God. You are like God's field. You are like God's building.

decisions.choice: are one: on the same level and with one purpose
decisions.reason: ἕν is neuter, "one thing": the planter and the waterer belong to one work. Neither stands above the other, so there is nothing to make parties over.

decisions.choice: wage: what God gives each worker at the end; it matches the labor, not the visible results
decisions.reason: μισθὸν is pay for work. κόπον is hard, tiring toil: God will reward faithful work, whatever its visible success. Verses 14-15 show that this reward is distinct from being saved.

decisions.choice: God's fellow workers: workers who belong to God and work together for him
alternatives: fellow workers with God, working alongside him
decisions.reason: θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί can mean that Paul and Apollos work together with God, or that they work together as God's workers. "God's" stands first in all three phrases (fellow workers, field, building), each time saying to whom something belongs; and verses 5-7 stress that the workers are only servants. So "belonging to God" is more likely, though the other reading is possible.

decisions.choice: field and building: pictures the Old Testament uses for God's people
decisions.reason: God promises to plant and to build his people (Jeremiah 1:10; 24:6). Paul now leaves the field and takes up the building, which he develops in verses 10-17.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}} own wage
decisions.reason: "Each" is each worker, and Paul's words apply to anyone who builds on the foundation (verse 10), so the default pronoun is inclusive.

decisions.choice: fellow workers in God's service
decisions.reason: Balanced states the reading chosen in m3; Literal keeps "God's fellow workers", which can be read either way.

decisions.choice: be rewarded (B); God will reward (R)
decisions.reason: "Wage" in Balanced and Readable would suggest earning salvation; the word is the pay a worker gets, and here it means God's reward (m2). Readable names God as the giver, which the passage implies.

decisions.choice: You are like God's field. You are like God's building.
alternatives: You are God's field, God's building.
decisions.reason: Readable marks the pictures as pictures.

records.source: Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων θεμέλιον ἔθηκα, ἄλλος δὲ ἐποικοδομεῖ.
records.gloss: According to the grace of the God the [one] given to me, as [a] wise master builder [a] foundation I laid, and another builds on [it].
pieces: Using the grace God gave me, I set a foundation in place like an expert builder, and another person is now building on top of it.

L.10: According to the grace of God that was given to me, like a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another is building on [it].

R.10: God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace gave me the work of a skilled builder, and I laid the foundation. Now another person is building on it.

decisions.choice: grace: God's gift of a calling and the ability to carry it out
decisions.reason: χάριν here is the grace that made Paul an apostle and gave him his work, as in Romans 15:15-16 and Galatians 2:9. He laid the foundation by God's gift, not his own skill.

decisions.choice: a skilled master builder: the expert in charge of a building project
alternatives: wise in the sense of the wisdom Paul has rejected in chapters 1-2
decisions.reason: ἀρχιτέκτων is the master builder who plans the work and directs the other builders. σοφὸς here means skilled at a craft, as the Greek Old Testament uses the word of the craftsmen who built the tabernacle (Exodus 31:6; 35:10). After chapters 1-2 the word also makes a point: this is the true kind of wisdom.

decisions.choice: laid a foundation: Paul began the church at Corinth
decisions.reason: Paul was the first to preach the gospel in Corinth (Acts 18:1-11; compare 4:15).

decisions.choice: another: whoever builds on after Paul, Apollos and others
decisions.reason: ἄλλος is general. It includes Apollos, but the warnings that follow apply to anyone who teaches and leads in the church.

decisions.choice: expert builder (B); skilled builder (R)
decisions.reason: "Wise" in current English is about good judgment; here the word means skill at a craft (m2). Literal keeps "wise".

decisions.choice: God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace gave me the work
alternatives: According to the grace of God given to me
decisions.reason: Readable makes God the subject, so that the sentence is short and plain.

records.heading: Building on the one foundation

records.source: ἕκαστος δὲ βλεπέτω πῶς ἐποικοδομεῖ·
records.gloss: But each let him watch how he builds on [it];
pieces: But each one must take care how to build on it.

L.10: But let each one watch how {{gender:they build|he builds}} on [it].

R.10: But everyone who builds must be careful how they do it.

decisions.choice: watch: take care, beware
decisions.reason: βλεπέτω is a warning, as in 8:9 and 10:12. Verses 12-15 explain why: the work will be tested.

decisions.choice: each: each one who builds on the foundation, that is, those who teach and lead in the church
decisions.reason: The context is the work of Paul, Apollos and other builders. Whether every believer is in view as well is debated; the warning applies most directly to those who teach.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they build|he builds}}
decisions.reason: "Each" is general, so the default pronoun is inclusive.

records.source: θεμέλιον γὰρ ἄλλον οὐδεὶς δύναται θεῖναι παρὰ τὸν κείμενον, ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός·
records.gloss: For [a] foundation other no one is able to lay besides the [one] lying, who is Jesus Christ;
pieces: For there is no other foundation anyone can lay; the one already in place is Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.11: For no one is able to lay another foundation besides the one lying [there], which is Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.11: The foundation is already there, and it is Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. No one can lay a different one.

decisions.choice: lying: already laid and in place
decisions.reason: κείμενον is a present participle: the foundation is there and stays there. Paul laid it by preaching Jesus Christ (2:2), but it is not his foundation; it is God's.

decisions.choice: the foundation is a person, Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: ὅς is "who": the foundation is Jesus Christ himself, crucified and risen, whom Paul preached (2:2; 15:3-4). Nothing built in the church can rest on anything else.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in the form of the name. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: The foundation is already there, and it is Jesus Christ. No one can lay a different one.
alternatives: No one can lay another foundation besides the one already laid
decisions.reason: Readable names the foundation first, so that the main point comes before the comparison.

records.source: εἰ δέ τις ἐποικοδομεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν θεμέλιον χρυσόν, ἄργυρον, λίθους τιμίους, ξύλα, χόρτον, καλάμην, ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον φανερὸν γενήσεται, ἡ γὰρ ἡμέρα δηλώσει· ὅτι ἐν πυρὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται, καὶ ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον ὁποῖόν ἐστιν τὸ πῦρ αὐτὸ δοκιμάσει.
records.gloss: Now if anyone builds on the foundation gold, silver, stones precious, wood, hay, straw, \v 13 of each the work evident will become, for the day will make [it] clear; because in fire it is revealed, and of each the work of what sort it is the fire itself will test.
pieces: If anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay or straw,
each builder's work will come out into the open. The Day will make it plain, since that Day arrives in fire, and the fire itself will prove what kind of work each one has done.

L.12: Now if anyone builds on the foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,
L.13: each one's work will become evident, for the Day will make [it] clear, because it is revealed with fire, and the fire itself will test of what sort each one's work is.

R.12: People may build on this foundation with gold, silver or fine stone. Or they may build with wood, hay or straw.
R.13: But one day everyone will see what kind of work each builder has done. On the day of judgment it will be made plain. That day will come with fire, and the fire will test what each person's work is really like.

decisions.choice: two kinds of material: costly and lasting, or cheap and burnable
decisions.reason: Gold, silver and costly stone were used in the finest buildings, above all temples; Solomon's temple was built of costly stones and overlaid with gold (1 Kings 5:17; 6:21-22). Wood, hay and straw were the stuff of poor houses: beams, thatch and filler. Fire tests the difference.

decisions.choice: precious stones: costly building stone, such as fine marble
decisions.reason: λίθους τιμίους can mean jewels, but in a list of building materials it most likely means valuable cut stone, as in 1 Kings 7:9-11. Isaiah 54:11-12 pictures the restored city built with jewels, so both ideas may be present.

decisions.choice: the Day: the day of judgment, when the Lord Jesus comes
alternatives: any day of trouble in this life
decisions.reason: Paul has already spoken of "the day of our Lord Jesus Christ" (1:8) and will say that the Lord will bring hidden things to light when he comes (4:5). The article marks it as the well-known day.

decisions.choice: it is revealed: the Day is revealed with fire
alternatives: the work is revealed by fire
decisions.reason: The subject of ἀποκαλύπτεται is not named. Most naturally it is the Day just mentioned: it comes with fire (2 Thessalonians 1:7-8). It could also be each one's work. The present tense describes what is certain to happen.

decisions.choice: fire as the picture of God's judgment
decisions.reason: The Old Testament pictures the day of the Lord as fire that tests and refines (Malachi 3:2-3; 4:1). Here the fire tests what kind of work each one has done; it is a picture, not a physical description.

decisions.choice: what is built: the teaching and work each one adds to the church
alternatives: the people brought into the church
decisions.reason: Paul does not say exactly what the materials stand for. In context the builders are those who teach and lead (verses 5-10), and the building is the church (verse 9), so the quality of their work in the church is tested. Some take the materials to be the converts themselves.

decisions.choice: the Day
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced capitalise "Day" to show it is the well-known day of judgment (m3); Readable says "the day of judgment".

decisions.choice: costly stones (B); fine stone (R)
decisions.reason: "Precious stones" in English means jewels; Balanced and Readable point to building stone (m2). Literal keeps "precious stones".

decisions.choice: short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence into five, and turns "if anyone builds" into a statement of what people may do.

records.source: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον μενεῖ ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν, μισθὸν λήμψεται·
records.gloss: If of anyone the work will remain which he built on, [a] wage he will receive;
pieces: If what someone has built on the foundation survives, that builder will receive a reward.

L.14: If anyone's work that {{gender:they|he}} built on [it] remains, {{gender:they|he}} will receive a wage.

R.14: If what a person has built is still standing after the fire, God will reward that person.

decisions.choice: remain: survive the testing fire
decisions.reason: μενεῖ is the opposite of "burned up" in verse 15: the work comes through the fire of the Day (verse 13).

decisions.choice: a reward for faithful work, distinct from salvation
decisions.reason: μισθὸν is the wage of verse 8. Verse 15 shows that a worker whose work burns is still saved, so the reward is something given in addition; Paul does not say what it is (compare 9:17-18 and Philippians 4:1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" is general, so the default pronoun is inclusive.

decisions.choice: reward
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, Balanced and Readable say "reward"; Literal keeps "wage".

decisions.choice: still standing after the fire; God will reward
decisions.reason: Readable says what the work survives (verse 13) and who gives the reward.

records.source: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον κατακαήσεται, ζημιωθήσεται, αὐτὸς δὲ σωθήσεται, οὕτως δὲ ὡς διὰ πυρός.
records.gloss: If of anyone the work will be burned up, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, yet so as through fire.
pieces: If someone's work burns up, that person will suffer loss. The builder will still be saved, but only as one who comes out through the fire.

L.15: If anyone's work is burned up, {{gender:they|he}} will suffer loss, but {{gender:they themselves|he himself}} will be saved, yet so as through fire.

R.15: If what a person has built burns up, that person will lose the reward. But God will still save that person, like someone who escapes from a burning house with nothing.

decisions.choice: suffer loss: lose what the work would have earned
decisions.reason: ζημιωθήσεται can mean to be fined or to suffer loss. Set against "will receive a reward" in verse 14 and "he himself will be saved" here, it means losing the reward, not losing salvation.

decisions.choice: he himself will be saved: the worker, as distinct from his work
decisions.reason: αὐτὸς stresses the person over against the work. σωθήσεται looks to final salvation at the Day.

decisions.choice: as through fire: barely, like someone escaping from a fire with nothing left
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures a person who gets out of a burning building alive but loses everything in it. The Old Testament has a similar picture: "a brand plucked from the fire" (Amos 4:11; Zechariah 3:2).

decisions.choice: the fire is the testing of the Day, not a process of cleansing
decisions.reason: In the passage the fire is the fire that comes with the Day and tests each one's work (verse 13). Paul describes that one moment of judgment; he does not describe a period of cleansing after death.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}; {{gender:they themselves|he himself}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" is general, so the default pronouns are inclusive.

decisions.choice: lose the reward; God will still save; escapes from a burning house with nothing
alternatives: suffer loss; will be saved; as through fire
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the loss (m1), names God as the one who saves, and explains the picture (m3). "Burning house" fills in the picture beyond the words, so reviewers should check that it does not say more than Paul does.

records.source: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ναὸς θεοῦ ἐστε καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν;
records.gloss: Not do you know that [a] temple of God you are and the Spirit of the God dwells in you?
pieces: Do you not know that together you are God's temple, and that God's Spirit lives among you?

L.16: Do you not know that you are God's temple and [that] the Spirit of God dwells in you?

R.16: Do you not know that all of you together are God's temple? God's own Spirit lives among you.

decisions.choice: do you not know: a rebuke; they should know this
decisions.reason: Paul uses this question ten times in the letter (3:16; 5:6; 6:2, 3, 9, 15, 16, 19; 9:13, 24), each time reminding them of something they already know but are not living by.

decisions.choice: temple: the sanctuary itself, the house where God lives
alternatives: the whole temple area with its courts
decisions.reason: ναὸς is the inner house of a temple, where the god was thought to live, not the outer courts. Corinth had many temples; for Paul the one true temple was the house of the God of Israel, where his presence dwelt (1 Kings 8:10-13).

decisions.choice: you together, the church, are God's temple
alternatives: each believer's body is a temple
decisions.reason: "You" is plural throughout, and the temple is one: the church as a whole is God's house, the place where his Spirit lives. In 6:19 Paul applies the same picture to each believer's body; here it is the church. Compare 2 Corinthians 6:16 and Ephesians 2:21-22.

decisions.choice: in you: among you as a people, and in each of you
decisions.reason: ἐν ὑμῖν with a plural can mean "among you" or "in you". With the church as the temple, "among you" is the main sense.

decisions.choice: together (B); all of you together (R); among you
alternatives: you are God's temple ... dwells in you
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural, and "in you" would suggest each person alone; Balanced and Readable make the plural plain (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: a second sentence
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question into a question and a statement.

records.heading: You are God's temple

records.source: εἴ τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φθείρει, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ θεός· ὁ γὰρ ναὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἅγιός ἐστιν, οἵτινές ἐστε ὑμεῖς.
records.gloss: If anyone the temple of the God destroys, will destroy this [one] the God; for the temple of the God holy is, which you are.
pieces: If anyone brings ruin on the temple of God, God will bring ruin on that person. The temple of God is holy, and you are that temple.

L.17: If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy that [person]; for the temple of God is holy, which you are.

R.17: If anyone ruins God's temple, God will ruin that person. God's temple is holy: it belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone. And you are that temple.

decisions.choice: destroy, ruin: the same verb for the sin and for God's judgment
decisions.reason: φθείρει and φθερεῖ are the same verb, which can mean to ruin, spoil or destroy. The punishment matches the deed: whoever wrecks God's temple, by dividing the church with rivalry and the world's wisdom, will be wrecked by God.

decisions.choice: holy: set apart for God and belonging to him
decisions.reason: ἅγιός describes what belongs to God and may not be treated as common. To ruin the temple is to sin against God himself.

decisions.choice: which you are: you are that temple
alternatives: and holy is what you are
decisions.reason: οἵτινές most likely refers to the temple: the holy temple is the Corinthians themselves, as verse 16 said. It could refer to "holy": they are holy, as the temple is. Either way, they belong to God.

decisions.choice: brings ruin on ... will bring ruin on
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the same verb twice, as the Greek does (m1); "ruin" covers both spoiling and destroying.

decisions.choice: it belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "holy" means here (m2).

records.source: Μηδεὶς ἑαυτὸν ἐξαπατάτω· εἴ τις δοκεῖ σοφὸς εἶναι ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ, μωρὸς γενέσθω, ἵνα γένηται σοφός, ἡ γὰρ σοφία τοῦ κόσμου τούτου μωρία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ἐστιν· γέγραπται γάρ· Ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν·
records.gloss: Let no one himself deceive; if anyone thinks wise to be among you in the age this, foolish let him become, so that he may become wise. \v 19 For the wisdom of the world this foolishness with the God is; for it has been written: The [one] catching the wise in the craftiness of them;
pieces: Let no one fool {{gender:themselves|himself}}. Anyone among you who thinks {{gender:they are|he is}} wise in this present age must become a fool in order to become wise.
What this world calls wisdom is foolishness in the eyes of God, for Scripture says, "He traps the wise in their own cleverness."

L.18: Let no one deceive {{gender:themselves|himself}}. If anyone among you thinks {{gender:they are|he is}} wise in this age, let {{gender:them|him}} become foolish, so that {{gender:they|he}} may become wise.
L.19: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it has been written, "[He is] the one catching the wise in their craftiness."

R.18: Do not fool yourselves. If any of you think you are wise by the standards of this present time, be willing to look foolish, so that you can become truly wise.
R.19: What this world thinks is wise, God thinks is foolish. The Scriptures say, "God catches wise people in their own clever tricks."

decisions.choice: let no one deceive himself: about the wisdom they prize
decisions.reason: The warning looks both back and forward: back to the danger of ruining God's temple (verse 17), and forward to those who think themselves wise (compare 8:2; Galatians 6:3).

decisions.choice: this age, this world: human life and its standards apart from God, which are passing away
decisions.reason: "This age" is the present order of things, which is coming to an end (1:20; 2:6-8). κόσμου τούτου here means the same: human society and the wisdom it values, not the created world as such (contrast verse 22).

decisions.choice: become foolish to become wise: accept the message the world calls foolish
decisions.reason: The world counts the message of the cross foolishness, but it is God's wisdom (1:18-25). To become wise, a person must give up the world's standards and accept that message, even if it makes them look foolish.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Job 5:13
decisions.reason: The words are from Job 5:13, where Eliphaz speaks of God, who catches the crafty in their own schemes. Paul's wording differs from the Greek Old Testament and stands closer to the Hebrew. The one who catches is God.

decisions.choice: the one catching: Paul quotes a phrase, not a whole sentence
decisions.reason: Ὁ δρασσόμενος is a participle, "the one who catches", lifted from its sentence in Job. It describes God.

decisions.choice: {{gender:themselves|himself}}; {{gender:they are|he is}}; {{gender:them|him}}; {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: "No one" and "anyone" are general, so the default pronouns are inclusive.

decisions.choice: Do not fool yourselves. If any of you think you
alternatives: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the readers directly, which is what "among you" implies and is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: Scripture says (B); The Scriptures say (R)
decisions.reason: "It has been written" is the usual way of citing Scripture; Balanced and Readable say so plainly. Literal keeps the form.

decisions.choice: God catches
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the subject in Job (m5).

records.heading: Become foolish to be wise

records.source: καὶ πάλιν· Κύριος γινώσκει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς τῶν σοφῶν ὅτι εἰσὶν μάταιοι.
records.gloss: And again: [The] Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are futile.
pieces: And again, "The Lord knows how empty the reasonings of the wise are."

L.20: And again, "[The] Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are futile."

R.20: And another passage says, "The Lord knows that the ideas of wise people are worth nothing."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 94:11
decisions.reason: The words are from Psalm 94:11 (93:11 in the Greek numbering). The psalm says the Lord knows the thoughts of human beings; Paul says "of the wise", applying the verse to his point. Reviewers should check the wording against the Greek Old Testament.

decisions.choice: Lord: in Psalm 94:11 this stands for God's own name, the LORD
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Psalm 94:11 the word is the divine name; the Greek Old Testament and Paul have Κύριος.

decisions.choice: futile: empty, achieving nothing
decisions.reason: μάταιοι describes what has no result or substance. The Greek of Ecclesiastes uses the related noun for what is "vanity", like a breath.

decisions.choice: knows the reasonings, that they are futile: knows that they are futile
decisions.reason: Greek often names the object first and then says what is known about it; the sense is that the Lord knows how futile their reasoning is.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: "The LORD" is kept for the divine name in the Old Testament itself. Paul quotes the psalm with the Greek word for "Lord", so English writes "Lord", as in John 1:23; m2 notes the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: another passage says
decisions.reason: Readable says what "again" refers to: a second passage of Scripture.

records.source: ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις· πάντα γὰρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν, εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα, πάντα ὑμῶν, ὑμεῖς δὲ Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸς δὲ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: So that let no one boast in human beings; for all things of you are, \v 22 whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or [the] world or life or death or things present or things coming, all of you, \v 23 and you of Christ, and Christ of God.
pieces: So let no one take pride in mere human beings. Everything is yours:
Paul or Apollos or Cephas, the world, life or death, what is here now or what is still to come. It all belongs to you,
and you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} belongs to God.

L.21: So let no one boast in human beings; for all things are yours,
L.22: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or [the] world or life or death or things present or things to come, all [are] yours,

R.21: So do not brag about following any human leader. Everything belongs to you.
R.22: Paul, Apollos and Peter all belong to you. The world, life and death, what is happening now and what will happen in the future: all of it is yours.
R.23: And you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} belongs to God.

decisions.choice: boast in human beings: take pride in human leaders and put confidence in them
decisions.reason: καυχάσθω is to boast or take pride in something. The Corinthians were boasting of the leaders they followed; Paul has already said that the only right boasting is in the Lord (1:31).

decisions.choice: all things are yours: the slogans turned around
decisions.reason: The Corinthians said "I am of Paul" (1:12; 3:4). Paul turns it around: Paul, Apollos and Cephas belong to the church, as servants given for its good.

decisions.choice: Cephas: the Aramaic name, meaning "rock", of the apostle Peter
decisions.reason: Jesus gave Simon this name (John 1:42). Paul usually calls him Cephas (1:12; 9:5; 15:5; Galatians 2:9).

decisions.choice: the world: the created order and everything in it
decisions.reason: In verse 19 the world is the human order with its false wisdom; here, in a list with life and death and the present and the future, it is the whole created world. All of it serves God's people, because they belong to Christ.

decisions.choice: things present and things to come: the present and the future
decisions.reason: ἐνεστῶτα and μέλλοντα are participles, "what is here" and "what is going to be". Romans 8:38 has the same pair.

decisions.choice: Christ belongs to God: as the Son who comes from the Father and does his work
alternatives: Christ is less than God in his nature
decisions.reason: Paul says something similar in 11:3 and 15:28, of the Son's relation to the Father and his work. He also calls Christ the one Lord through whom all things exist (8:6). The point here is the chain of belonging: the church does not belong to its leaders but to Christ, and through Christ to God.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal writes "{{christos:Christ|Messiah}}'s" for the possessive.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Young readers know the apostle as Peter, so Readable uses that name here as it does in 1:12 (m3).

decisions.choice: take pride in mere human beings (B); brag about following any human leader (R)
decisions.reason: "Boast in" is not natural English. Readable says what the boasting was about (m1).
